header:
# Progress — run `agent-harness-2026-10-26` (agent-harness)

What this file is: the run's journal, rendered from `entries.jsonl` after every session, newest entry first (the driver's own notes are `harness-log.md`). Each entry says what one session did, what passed, what it found (discoveries) and what it needs from you (questions).

The spec is `docs/specs/2026-10-26-lanes.md` with `docs/specs/2026-10-26-suite-split.md` as its P0. Milestones: P0 the suite split (tests/lib.sh, tests/checks/ one file per section, a parallel runner, the conformance fixture, CHECK_KEY_IGNORE) · P1 lanes at MAX_LANES=1 (the record on its own branch harness/<run>, code on harness-lane/<run>/<m> in a slot, lib/lane.sh as the milestone process, the coordinator) · P2 two lanes (admission by memory and five-hour headroom, the re-base rule, slots and gc, the record PR, status and summary). P1 waits for P0, P2 for P1. Each verified milestone merges into `main` by itself.

How to read the feature list: `feature_list.json` lists features in priority order; `passes` is the session's claim, the verify entry for a milestone is what counts. Steps are the checks a verifier re-runs; the last is always a green suite. From P1 on every new check goes in a `tests/checks/` file by topic and its name into `tests/fixtures/check-names.txt`.

To steer: edit `INBOX.md` on this branch (GitHub app). Line 1 `status: pause` or `status: stop` takes effect before the next session; answers go under `## Answers`. Sessions never park on this run (the brief): they take the spec's default and record it in the decision file. After the run: set `MAX_LANES=2` in `~/.config/harness/config.sh` before the next run starts.

discoveries.text: The suite is one file, tests/run.sh (1634 lines, 50 `# ---- <title> ----` sections, 325 checks, all names unique and environment-independent) and takes about 10 min single-threaded on this box (init measured 597 s), so every session spends 10 min per full run until P0-02 lands; iterate on a subset (`bash lib/check.sh <args>` is never cached) and run the full suite once before flipping passes.

The pre-split suite output of this run's init is at /tmp/harness/agent-harness/agent-harness-2026-10-26/check.out (325 PASS lines): P0-01 generates tests/fixtures/check-names.txt from it instead of re-running the monolith.

Sections known to read an earlier section's state: run 15e (line 1145) reads $T/demo-hlog.md from run 1 (line 540); the gc section (755) and runs 2-14 reuse run 1's demo repo and tags; the eval sections share $ED; the debrief sections share a runner log. split.sh's grouping pairs are found by running each file alone, never by patching a check.

The driver loop is lib/driver.sh:567-719 (counters n, limits, repairs, gated as shell variables; verify_ready before each pick); verify is at 375, merge_one 314, merge_milestones 351, finish 484, restrict 87 (the revert pattern for a commit touching the record). bin/harness: cmd_continue 212, cmd_merge 227, cmd_status 236, cmd_gc 351 with record_only at 384 and the harness/ + harness-merge/ prefix passes at 449.

Helpers that already exist for the lanes work: `notify.mjs question <before> <after>` computes the INBOX lines a session added; `features.mjs` has unpass, repair, snapshot, milestone-done, touched-outside; scope.sh has mem_available_gb's reader (HARNESS_MEMINFO), scope_unit and scope_owns (role regex at line 27); metrics.mjs `usage` reads unifiedWindows from the real capture tests/fixtures/usage-limit.jsonl, which carries five_hour beside seven_day.

The stubs: tests/stub-claude.sh acts on the prompt's first line and STUB_* flags (set with `tmux set-environment -g` for sessions started in tmux, plain env otherwise); tests/stub-gh.sh keeps PRs as files under $STUB_DIR/prs and really merges into the bare origin; the record of git pushes is the bare origin itself. New stub behaviour must copy a real shape (fakes mirror the live API).

S4 of the suite-split spec (`--for` selection by `# covers:`) is deliberately not in the list: P1 and P2 are the run's bulk and a feature a milestone can't ship without would hold P0. It is a one-session interactive change if wanted.

questions: S4 (`tests/run.sh --for <paths>` by `# covers:` lines) was left out of P0 so the split ships first; default taken: skip it this run, do it interactively if the two-minute suite still feels slow to iterate on.
P1 keeps the lane port equal to the run port (one lane); distinct per-lane ports arrive with admission in P2-02. Default taken: no port change until two lanes exist.
